messages:
carmen: Observed a weird split: hosted rollout metrics look fine, but Dedicated p95 for the premium pools jumped ~3x after the rollout. No user 5xxs yet but latency is visible to customers on the premium tier.

deploy-bot: ALERT: cohort-delta detected. Dedicated pool 'premium-eu' p95 > 400ms. Suggested action: partial-rollback -> dedicated:v1.9.7 (confidence 0.65). Autorevert scheduled for affected pool in 2m unless suppressed.

tyler: interesting. So this is Dedicated-only? Hosted customers not affected?

carmen: correct. Hosted is stable. Telemetry shows scheduling pressure on premium-eu VM families and increased tail latency tied to a kernel scheduling tweak that only runs on Dedicated images.

ops-ana: can confirm logs show higher context-switch counts on premium-eu. We can revert the dedicated image or apply a kernel hotpatch. Hotpatch has lower blast radius.

amanda-cs: AMP accounts on premium-eu might see latency. I'll ping account teams and prepare a customer note template.

lee-oncall: proposal: allow deploy-bot to autorevert on Dedicated pools only, suppress autorevert for hosted. That lets us quickly remediate affected customers while leaving hosted rollout to continue. Thoughts?

tyler: need to be careful with split versions: routing compatibility ok? v1.9.7 -> v1.10.0 difference minor, should be fine for Dedicated routing.

carmen: agree with lee. Ops Ana, what's ETA to perform dedicated rollback vs hotpatch?

ops-ana: dedicated rollback command: `releases rollback --to v1.9.7 --scope dedicated --pools premium-eu` 30s to run. Hotpatch path: `opsctl patch kernelcfg --unset sched_backpressure_v2 --pools premium-eu` 2m and rolling restart ~6m. Hotpatch likely faster and safer.

amanda-cs: if we do a Dedicated-only rollback it might trigger customer confusion because hosted will continue on the newer version. We should include that in the customer blurb and CC account owners before executing.

deploy-bot: NOTE: autorevert options: `deploybot autorevert --scope dedicated --pools premium-eu` (will run in 90s) or `deploybot suppress-autorevert --scope hosted` to keep hosted stable.

lee-oncall: decision: apply kernel hotpatch to premium-eu first (lower risk), monitor 10m. If perf not recovered, run dedicated rollback. Carmen, Ana, please run hotpatch; Tyler coordinate CS comms. I'll keep autorevert suppressed for hosted and allow deploy-bot to act on dedicated pool if we don't get improvement.

carmen: applying hotpatch now: `opsctl patch kernelcfg --unset sched_backpressure_v2 --pools premium-eu --reason "Dedicated p95 regression"`

ops-ana: executing...

ops-ana: ```
patch applied: sched_backpressure_v2 unset (pools: premium-eu)
restarting premium-eu-01 ... ok
restarting premium-eu-02 ... ok
restarting premium-eu-03 ... ok
```

deploy-bot: MONITOR: post-hotpatch p95 on premium-eu dropped from ~420ms -> ~130ms within 4m. Autorevert suppressed for hosted; dedicated autorevert remaining enabled.

amanda-cs: notifying account teams: "We applied a targeted fix to your dedicated pool; you may briefly see improved latency. No further action required." Draft posted and sent to owners.

lee-oncall: recommendation: keep hosted suppression for another 60m to avoid flip-flop, keep dedicated autorevert enabled for 15m in case other pools flare. Carmen, if metrics hold for 15m, unpin and document in release notes that we applied a hotpatch to Dedicated pool only.

carmen: metrics stable across premium-eu for 20m now. Marking this as resolved for now. Creating rollback ticket ops-RB-1715558888 as part of runbook (will close if no follow-up). Postmortem owner: @carmen, draft due EOD.

tyler: updating release notes: "Targeted kernel hotpatch applied to Dedicated 'premium-eu' pools due to latency regression; hosted rollout unaffected. Autorevert suppressed for hosted to preserve monitoring signal."

amanda-cs: customer notes sent and account teams acknowledged.

lee-oncall: closing the thread once postmortem link posted. Thanks everyone.
